newsitem.title: USA: After 58 years, Superman to get married.
newsitem.headline: After 58 years, Superman to get married.

text.p: Talk about fear of commitment. After 58 years of playing coy, 58 years of endless dithering and denial, 58 years of dating the same woman, Superman is finally going to get married.
The lucky woman is Lois Lane, one of only four people in Metropolis to know the Man of Steel's super-secrets -- that he has a split personality, is not human and has come back once from the dead.

The wedding between Lane and Superman, who will be dressed up at the nuptials as his mild-mannered alter-ego, Clark Kent, will take place in the Oct. 9 issue of Superman Comics and three days earlier on the TV series, "Lois and Clark, the New Adventures of Superman."

They have been dating on and off since 1938, when the comic book began, and formally became engaged in 1990. Even though it is 1996 and they have been together 58 years, they still maintain separate apartments.
They are getting married "because they decided it was the right thing to do. It just took them a while, about 60 years," Mike Carlin, executive editor of DC Comics, said on Tuesday.
Carlin, who oversaw the killing off of Superman in 1992 and his long, complicated resurrection a year later, said the wedding will be "nice."

"Superman needs a break after all these years of fighting bad guys, stopping trains, dying and coming back, saving the planet etc.," Carlin said. But he cautioned, "That doesn't mean he is going to survive his honeymoon in Hawaii."

Well, you know he will, even though the honeymoon will last three weeks, enough to test any marriage, even a Superhero's. In Hawaii the couple will have to contend with something called "the ancient menace of Kekona," a problem other Hawaii honeymooners have somehow managed to avoid.
Carlin said the wedding will be preceded by his and hers pre-nuptial parties at which fights break out as if to "prove the couple are perfect for each other."
Lex Luthor, Superman's nemesis, is lurking about and "figures in the story." So does Lois's father, who is opposed to the marriage because he thinks Clark Kent is not good enough for his daughter.
The plot team at DC Comics has not figured out yet how the marriage will go -- small things like whether the couple will have children or a set of China stamped with the letter "S."
"We know aliens and humans can have children. We have the example of Mr Spock from Star Trek," Carlin said. Superman is an alien immigrant, the last survivor of the planet Krypton.

Although the couple will have their share of toil and strife, sources say a divorce is out of the question. "They are not Charles and Diana. Anyone who believes in truth, justice and the American Way cannot get a divorce," a source close to the couple's drawingboard said.
When DC Comics killed Superman in 1992, it sold some six million copies of an issue with black mourning satin on the cover. Its plans for the marriage issue are satin-free.
The "Wedding Album" issue will have a white cardboard cover with the letter "S" embossed on it and will sell for $4.95.
